answer: An agent economy can admit newcomers in small cohorts drawn at random each epoch and bound by joint liability: each cohort stakes together on one island of shared collateral, and if any member is caught farming, the whole cohort's stake is slashed. A farm cannot quarantine its risk — each extra fake raises the chance its cohort is the one audited, and the river of expected loss runs through every head it adds. One marble of proof against a single fake cracks the whole cohort, so the price of the next identity is the entire cohort's stake, and it climbs with every head.
